newsitem.title: UK: Dolly the sheep gets a competitor - rice.
newsitem.headline: Dolly the sheep gets a competitor - rice.

text.p: Dolly the sheep could have a competitor -- not a genetically engineered animal, but a field of rice, New Scientist reported on Thursday.
It said a U.S. company had found a way to genetically engineer rice that will produce human proteins -- the same aim of the scientists who shocked the world by cloning Dolly.
Applied Phytologics of Davis, California, has developed rice that can produce alpha-1-antitrypsin, a human protein used to treat cystic fibrosis, the magazine reported.
The rice will be ready for harvest in September, and the scientists at the company hope to extract the protein by malting the rice.

"I think it's going to dawn on the industry shortly that in plant biotechnology cereal grains are going to be the crop to work with," Raymond Rodriguez, chairman of Applied Phytologics, told the magazine.

The researchers at Scotland's Roslin Institute and PPL Therapeutics Plc are testing their version of alpha-1-antitrypsin (AAT) in human volunteers. They have genetically engineered sheep to produce it in their milk.
They are also working on human blood factors in their herds of transgenic animals.
But Applied Phytologics is working to produce many of the same proteins in plants and says its processes are more economical, New Scientist said.
